problem:
Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $F(x,y)={e}^{x}\,i+\operatorname{ln}⁡y\,j$ and $C$ is the line segment traversed from the point $A(3,2)$ to the point $B(1,5)?$

*Hint: Use the parametrization $r(t)=(3-2t)\,i+(2+3t)\,j.$*

activity_context.topic_title: Line Integrals of Vector-Valued Functions Over General Curves

feedback.problem: Evaluate ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $F(x,y)=(x+y)\,i+\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡\pi y\,j$ and $C$ is the line segment traversed from the point $A(1,-1)$ to the point $B(-3,1).$
feedback.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we need to parameterize the line segment.
The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are $a=i-j$ and $b=-3\,i+j.$
So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =a+t(b-a) \\  & =(i-j)+t[-3\,i+j-(i-j)] \\  & =(i-j)+t(-4\,i+2\,j) \\  & =(1-4t)\,i+(2t-1)\,j,\end{aligned}
$$

where $t$ varies from $t=0$ (at the point $A$) to $t=1$ (at the point $B$).
Thus, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=1-4t,\,y=2t-1.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =(x+y)\,i+\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡\pi y\,j \\  & =(1-4t+(2t-1))\,i+\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡((2t-1)\pi )\,j \\  & =-2t\,i+\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡((2t-1)\pi )\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-4t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t-1)j \\  & =-4\,i+2\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(-2t\,i+\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡((2t-1)\pi )\,j)\cdot (-4\,i+2j) \\  & =-2t\cdot (-4)+\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡((2t-1)\pi )\cdot 2 \\  & =8t+2\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡((2t-1)\pi ).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{1}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}8t+2\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡((2t-1)\pi )\,dt \\  & ={4{t}^{2}+\operatorname{sin}⁡((2t-1)\pi )|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =(4+\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi )-(0+\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\pi )) \\  & =(4+0)-(0+0) \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$
